Co-op:
{{disambig msg|co-op babies|the monster|Baby|items that follow Isaac|familiar}} Rebirth features 2 player local '''co-op''' on PC. The Afterbirth DLC increased this to 4 player local co-op. The PlayStation 4 and Steam versions of the game are capable of both local and online multiplayer via PS4's "Share Play" and Steam's "Remote Play Together" features, as well as a dedicated online multiplayer system. (These versions can also support up to 4 players.) Co-op players can join in at any time as a random baby, taking a Red Heart container away from Isaac and giving it to the second player. Subsequent pressing of the join button will despawn the baby, giving Isaac the Red Heart container back. Babies share Isaac's stats except for health and damage; babies deal half of Isaac's damage. Babies always have flight, but they cannot interact with objects like items and pickups, except for certain special babies like Magnet Baby and Isaac 2. {{dlc|a}} Joining as a co-op baby will bring up a menu that allows the player to pick from 5 special babies. Dying as one of the available special babies will remove it from the pool. {{dlc|r}} If you start a normal game and player 2/3/4 presses Start while in the starting room, a mini character selection wheel displays at the top of the screen, with which that player can choose any unlocked character, or a random character. If a player dies without any revival items, they become a ghost baby that can only deal minimal damage and press buttons. Once the boss of a floor is killed, the dead player is reborn with all the items they once had, but with half a heart. When a boss is killed, the item pedestal will spawn as many items as there are players. All players share resources (coins, bombs, and keys), but each have their own hearts and items. All damage players do to bosses is reduced by 20%, including the damage from items, familiars, or bombs. Once all players die, it's game over. {{dlc|r}}There are currently 604 babies in total. == Notes (Co-op Babies) == * [[Soul Heart]]s will be given to Player 2 before normal hearts, and half hearts will be given before full hearts. If player 2 dies, they can rejoin the game at the cost of another Red [[Heart container]], as a new random Baby. * The appearance of a majority of the co-op babies is solely cosmetic, but there are several "special" babies with beneficial effects. However, some special babies have detrimental effects. * The last [[shooting familiar]] Isaac picked up will follow Player 2 instead of Isaac. * If Isaac has more than 6 total hearts, including Soul Hearts and Black Hearts, Player 2 will take two hearts instead of one. * If Isaac has a maximum of 12 hearts, including Soul Hearts and Black Hearts, Player 2 will take three hearts instead of one or two. * The maximum amount of hearts Player 2 can have is three Red Hearts and one Soul Heart, using {{i|Scapular}}. ** {{dlc|a}} This limit increases by one Red Heart container, Soul Heart, or Black Heart when using Red Baby, Blue Baby, or Black Baby, respectively. * Because at least 1.5 hearts are required for co-op, Player 2 cannot join when playing as {{c|The Lost}}. * On the Nintendo Switch, you must restart the game after setting up the controllers or the join button will not work. == {{dlc|r}}Strategy (True Co-op) ==

Internally, pills are given a class from 0 to 3 and a polarity that reflects their influence: Pills in class 0 have little to no impact on a run overall, while pills in higher classes are correspondingly more influential, class 3 pills having effects as significant as permanent stat changes. Classes that end with + or - denote a positive or negative effect, otherwise considered neutral. This mechanic is used to balance the pill pool and avoid having too many negative or positive pills. The '''Boss Rush''' is an optional [[room]] that becomes available by beating [[Mom]] in {{s|Depths}}, {{s|Necropolis}}, or {{s|Dank Depths}} within 20 minutes, or {{dlc+|r}}beating her in {{s|Mausoleum}} or {{s|Gehenna}} within 25 minutes.{{dlc-}}

In the center of a large room, there will be 4 random [[item]]s to choose from (Picked from the [[Treasure Room (Item Pool)|Treasure Room item pool]]). Picking up an item will cause the other three to disappear and start the Boss Rush. Completing the Boss Rush will also reward 1 more item, separate from the 4 seen when first entering the room.

{{dlc|a}} There is a chance that there will only be 2 items to choose from. Additionally, items may be trapped behind [[rock]]s or [[spikes]]. Items may appear in the corners of the room instead of the center.

{{dlc|a+}} There is a small chance that there will be 8 items to choose from.

The Boss Rush consists of 15 waves with 2 [[boss]]es per wave. The next wave does not spawn until both bosses from the previous wave have been killed, and any lingering [[monster]]s from previous waves will not prevent the next wave from spawning.

Occasionally, all the bosses fought in the Boss Rush will be their [[Champion]] variants, if they have one.

== Notes ==
* If Mom is beaten within 20 minutes and Isaac enters the Angel or Devil Room, he must return to the boss room before 20 minutes have passed; otherwise, the Boss Rush entrance will be closed.
** If Isaac is teleported to the Devil Room while inside the Boss Rush room (for example, using a {{p|Joker}} card), exiting the Devil Room will lead him to Mom's Boss Room.
* If Isaac dies during the Boss Rush, but is able to respawn, the entrance to the Boss Rush room will still be open if the timer is still under 20 minutes. If the Boss Rush entrance has closed, the room can still be re-entered by dying in the Mom boss fight room at the cost of another life.
* The Boss Rush can only be retried by picking up an item off a pedestal in its room. If the item Isaac originally picked from the room was an active item and Isaac had another item to swap it for, the pedestal and item it was swapped out for will still be there. Swapping the items again will restart the fight. Alternatively, a new pedestal can be created, such as through a {{p|XX - Judgement}} card, {{dlc+|a+}} or dropping your active item via {{T|Butter!}} and taking its item will also restart the fight{{dlc-}}. {{dlc+|a+}} Also, having {{I|Broken Shovel 1}} in your possession will automatically start the Boss Rush if left and entered again.{{dlc-}}
* {{dlc+|a}} If a {{E|Grab Bag}} spawns for whatever reason, picking it up will start the Boss Rush. The player can still pick up one of the pedestal items.{{dlc-}}
* The boss rush does not unlock anything if beaten in a challenge.
* {{dlc+|a+}} Using {{i|Void}}, {{p|Black Rune}}, {{i|Abyss}}, or {{i|Moving Box|force=r}} will start the Boss Rush.{{dlc-}}
* If a {{E|chest}} is opened in the Boss Rush room, it will start the Boss Rush.
* {{i|Mama Mega!}} will open the Boss Rush room even if the time limit has expired. Leaving the room will cause the door to close if the time limit has expired.
* {{dlc+|a+}} Holding {{i|Broken Shovel 1}} will also open the Boss Rush room, ignoring the time limit, to complete {{i|Mom's Shovel}}.{{dlc-}}
* If a Crawl Space is entered from within the Boss Rush room, exiting the Crawl Space will not return the player to the Boss Rush room, but will instead place the player back in the Mom Boss Room.
* {{dlc+|r}} When {{i|Suplex!}} is used while a {{i|Berserk!}} effect is active, Isaac lands with an explosion similar to {{i|Mama Mega!}}. This explosion can open the boss rush door after the time limit has expired.{{dlc-}}
* {{i|Dad's Key}} can't open the door from the outside, but can open it from the inside, which can be used for taking an item, then leaving without fighting the bosses, for example.
* Despite being similar to a Mama Mega explosion, {{e|Giga Bomb}}s can't open the boss rush door.

== Tips ==
* The player's playtime can be checked at any moment by pressing TAB (or long-pressing SELECT on the controller), enabling Extra HUD in the options menu, or by simply looking down to the bottom screen on the 3DS version, where it is shown on the map.
* Each boss will always drop {{E|Red Heart|display=Hearts}} on normal difficulty, {{dlc|r}} and sometimes on hard difficulty. {{i|Dark Bum}} can turn red hearts from these drops into {{E|Soul Heart|nr}} ({{E|Black Heart|r}}s), providing loads of extra health.
* Take out {{E|Carrion Queen}} quickly, as its {{E|red poop}}s will remain for the rest of the boss rush. They can be advantageous though, as other bosses can also take damage from these poops. In particular, bouncing bosses like {{E|The Hollow}} and {{E|The Husk}} can quickly kill themselves on contact.
* All bosses with a {{i|Brimstone}} laser attack could severely hurt or even one-shot-kill each other, especially {{E|The Gate|}}. It may be beneficial to focus on the other boss before killing them.
* {{dlc|na}}Wave 9 can be quite difficult, as {{E|Monstro II}} (he always spawns on the left side) can catch the player off-guard with an offscreen {{i|Brimstone}} laser. The [[black creep]] left by {{E|Gish}} will remain until he is killed.
* {{dlc|na}}{{E|The Bloat}} + {{E|Mask of Infamy}} is one of the hardest waves, but {{E|The Bloat}} can be baited into destroying both the heart and the mask itself of the {{E|Mask of Infamy}} with its {{i|Brimstone}} lasers.
* Any teleport effect (such as [[card]]s, activated items, Telepills, etc) can be used to leave the Boss Rush. This can be used to gain one item without having to fight any bosses.
** {{dlc+|r}} After unlocking {{a|A Strange Door}}, [[Rocks#Marked Skulls|Marked Skulls]] will always appear on Depths II and will always drop {{p|0 - The Fool}}, providing a guaranteed way to escape Boss Rush.{{dlc-}}

The Harbingers:
'''The Harbingers''' is the achievement that unlocks {{e|Famine}}, {{e|War}}, {{e|Pestilence}}, and {{e|Death}} as four additional bosses. '''The Harbingers''' are referenced in the Bible as [[wikipedia:Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse|the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse]]. These bosses are only unlocked once {{e|Mom}} has been defeated for the first time. These bosses, with the exception of {{e|Conquest}} and {{e|Headless Horseman}}, are guaranteed to drop either a {{i|Ball of Bandages}} or a {{i|Cube of Meat}}. By default, there is a 10% chance the current floor's boss will be a Harbinger unless the floor has a fixed boss (for example, {{e|Mom}} in {{s|Depths}} and {{s|Necropolis}}) or the Harbinger has been fought already. By using the {{i|Book of Revelations}} on a floor, it is guaranteed that the boss will be a Harbinger.

== Trivia ==
* {{e|Conquest}} was added in the ''Binding of Isaac: Wrath of the Lamb''. In [[Wikipedia:Book of Revelation|the Bible]], Conquest is actually the first Horseman to appear, while {{e|Pestilence}} is a Horseman existing only in popular culture, coming from a different translation of the Greek word 'Thanatos', often meaning {{e|Death}} instead (the canon four Horsemen, thus, are Conquest, War, Famine and Death).
** {{e|Conquest}}'s entry in the secrets is called "The Forgotten Horseman", because of that very reason.
* {{e|Death}} is the only horseman specifically given a name in ''The Book of Revelation''.
* The use of the {{i|Book of Revelations}} item to summon a horseman for the current floor is reference to the fact that the book of the Bible in which the horsemen are described is Revelation.
* None of the Harbingers have a death animation.
* Under normal circumstances, {{e|Conquest}} and {{e|Headless Horseman}} are 2 of only 5 bosses (the others being {{e|Krampus}}, {{e|The Fallen}}, and {{e|Baby Plum}} if spared) who drop or can drop active items upon defeat.

'''Backasswards''' is challenge #31. Isaac starts on the {{E|Mega Satan}} boss fight with 8-10 random items and 10 Heart Containers (exact number may vary based on the items). The goal is to play the floors backwards, hence the challenge's namesake. Every floor ascended will cost one Heart Container (if the player has no Red Hearts, it will take a Soul Heart instead), and the oldest item in the inventory. However, if isaac has only one heart, isaac keeps the heart to prevent him from dying. The player starts each floor with a boss fight (except the {{s|Dark Room}}, which can be immediately completed), and will have to find the "starting room" to ascend a beam of light to the "previous" floor, similar to the effect of {{I|Dad's Note}}.

== Difficulty ==
Starting with a random selection of items, ''and'' starting on the {{E|Mega Satan}} boss fight makes this challenge very difficult at first. If Mega Satan and {{E|Satan}} can be defeated, the rest of the challenge becomes significantly easier. However, no bosses need to be defeated to progress - teleporting out of boss rooms can make the challenge much easier. While treasure rooms are disabled in this challenge, bosses will still offer a reward upon defeating them.

== Strategy ==
* Try to get some really powerful few-item synergies. Resetting is a perfectly good way to ensure good items.
** Since Isaac will have at least 10 Red Heart containers from the start, {{i|Pyromaniac}} and items that grant exploding shots ({{i|Ipecac}}, {{i|Dr. Fetus}}, and {{i|Epic Fetus}}) combined is game breaking since as long as he gets caught by his explosions, he can heal indefinitely. They also do plentiful damage to enemies and can open closed doors. Isaac also can heal from Mega Satan's {{dlc|nr}}rock waves and mini-bosses spawned by him which spawn ignited {{E|Bomb}}s, {{E|Troll Bomb}}s or {{E|Mega Troll Bomb}}s.
** Having {{i|Gnawed Leaf}} and something that can do damage while not moving, such as {{i|Daddy Longlegs}}, {{i|Dead Bird}}, or {{i|Smart Fly}}, can basically guarantee an eventual win. Damaging orbitals are also a big help. Finally, size-decreasing items, such as {{i|Pluto}} or items that block bullets, such as {{i|Trinity Shield}} will drastically reduce the difficulty of most of Mega Satan's attacks.
** {{i|The Wafer}} is an extremely useful item to receive in this challenge as well.
* Even without powerful items or synergies, the challenge of Mega Satan (or any other boss) can be skipped by teleporting out of the room. 
** Isaac only needs a starting item that produces a tarot card on pickup, such as {{I|Magic 8 Ball}} or {{I|Starter Deck}}. {{I|Booster Pack}} has a high chance to produce a card that can teleport Isaac since it spawns 5 random cards. {{P|0 - The Fool}}, {{P|IX - The Hermit}}, and {{P|XVIII - The Moon}} are all viable teleportation cards.
** {{I|Cursed Eye}} also works as a method of teleportation, but can come with the downside of unwanted teleportation.
** Teleportation through resurrection by means of items like the {{I|Ankh}} is possible but dangerous since most resurrection items revive Isaac with very low health.
* Taking a hit from {{E|Mom's Hand}} brings Isaac to the starting room of a floor. 
* Going up a floor will remove one heart container and one passive item. If Isaac only has one red heart container, something as simple as leaving the floor itself will end the run.
** For this reason, be wary of taking devil deals at low health.
** {{I|Dead Cat}} in particular can be a run-ender, as it removes all but one red heart container on pickup. Additionally, starting with this item will make the Mega Satan fight extremely hard due to the large health reduction it causes.
** Beware of {{i|Experimental Treatment}} too, as it has a chance to remove heart containers.
** {{E|Soul Heart}}s and {{E|Black Heart}}s are not affected by this if Isaac has any red heart containers. Thus, {{i|Guppy's Paw}} is an extremely useful item for this run.
* Shops spawn as normal above {{s|Womb}}.
* {{p|Rune of Ehwaz}} and {{i|We Need To Go Deeper!}} generate closed exits to the next floor, so they cannot help Isaac skip the current floor.
* Items to be removed first are the "first" items picked up. This is the item in the rightmost column, in the lowest row of that column. If powerful items are shown there, it is best to restart.
* {{dlc+|nr}} If a {{M|Mom's Dressing Table}} spawns in the starting room, its icon will show up on the map even if the starting room has not been visited yet. This makes finding the passage to the previous floor significantly easier.{{dlc-}}
* {{dlc+|r}} Items that spawn effects in the starting room of a floor (such as {{I|Card Reading}} and {{I|The Stairway}}) will have no effect in this challenge, as they disappear once Isaac is in any room other than the starting room.{{dlc-}}

== Notes ==
* As this challenge uniquely starts at Mega Satan, this challenge can be used as a convenient way to practice battling Mega Satan if you're still unfamiliar with the fight.
* Teleporting to the {{S|Dark Room}} through {{R|Sacrifice Room}} brings Isaac back to Mega Satan's fight, and all previously encountered floors will be regenerated.
* {{i|Halo of Flies}} will take two entire floors to be removed. Only one fly will be lost per floor.
* {{i|R Key}} will teleport Isaac back to the Mega Satan fight.
* {{dlc+|r}} Using {{I|Genesis}} after Dark Room may softlock a run, because the exit generated in the bedroom is closed. Escaping the room is possible if any item or pickup that allows escaping is generated. (eg. {{i|Teleport!}}, {{i|Forget Me Now}}){{dlc-}}
* {{E|The Lamb}} cannot be encountered in the Dark Room.
* Only {{i|The Negative}} can be picked up after defeating {{E|Mom}}.

'''Home''' is  the final floor of ''The Binding of Isaac'' as a whole''.'' It is one of the final floors alongside the {{s|Chest}}, the {{s|Dark Room}}, {{dlc|a+}}{{s|The Void}}, and the {{s|Corpse}}. It was added in ''[[The Binding of Isaac: Repentance]]''.

Home can be accessed after picking up {{i|Dad's Note}} and going through the [[ascent]] or by using the {{i|Glowing Hourglass}} in the first floor's starting room without entering any other rooms. The bosses of the floor are always {{e|Dogma}}, followed by {{e|The Beast|force=n}}.

== Layout ==
The Home floor has no enemies, and is completely empty. Similar to {{s|???}} and the [[Greed Mode|Greed mode]] floors, its layout is always the same. Home features Isaac's room, two corridors, a room with a pickup, the living room, and Mom's room.

Isaac's room is where Isaac spawns upon entering the stage. It contains a bed in the upper left corner and a carpet in the center, like a regular [[Bedroom]], as well as a {{E|Locked Chest}}. Isaac can sleep in his bed to recover provided he's not at full health, or to add three {{e|Soul Heart}}s provided he has no {{e|Red Heart}} containers. Triggering an explosion on the carpet will cause it to be damaged, but reveal nothing underneath.

A single door in the bottom wall leads to the narrow right corridor. Through a door in the upper side of the right wall is a small room that contains a random [[pickup]] or, rarely, an [[item]]. Further down in the left wall, there is another door leading to the house's living room.

The living room is double-sized and extends vertically downwards from the entrances at either side. It contains a large turned-off TV, placed against its northern wall, and a couch further south, as well as a red carpet located between them with a massive picture of a cross with wings. A door in the upper left side leads to another narrow corridor, which Isaac can walk north to reach Mom's room.

Mom's room contains a unique chest, a carpet, a dressing table, and Mom's bed — all of them larger than similar items found throughout the game. When the chest is opened for the first time, it will contain the {{i|Red Key}}, which will be permanently unlocked. In subsequent playthroughs, it draws from [[Mom's Chest (Item Pool)|its own item pool]] of Mom related items; the Red Key can still be found, but more rarely. The carpet and the dressing table in this room cannot be interacted with.

Sleeping in Mom's bed will cause Isaac to have a nightmare, showing the loading screen with no floor icons. In the dream, Isaac is sitting next to his mother as she watches TV. Isaac's distorted face then appears on the TV screen, as the noise of static begins to increase in volume.

After a flash of static briefly covering the entire screen, Isaac wakes up again, presumably at night since Home is considerably darker. At this point, when exiting Mom's room and walking down the left corridor, a grey light can be seen through the bottom-right door. The source of this light is the TV in the living room, which is now turned on but only emits static. Stepping on the cross in the living room's carpet will begin the battle against Home's first boss, Dogma.

Upon beating Dogma, a cutscene will play — then the fight with The Beast will start.

=== Hidden closet ===
In the hallway leading to Mom's bedroom, using either the {{i|Red Key}}, {{p|Cracked Key}}, or {{P|Soul of Cain}} will open up a hidden room. This is hinted by the existence of the closet on the other side of the map, by Isaac's bedroom. There is also a barely visible glowing red outline for the hidden door when the Red Key or Cracked Key has been picked up. The closet is also the place Isaac is thrown into in [[Endings|ending 21]].

Inside is the tainted version of the character currently being played, laying on the floor, crying. Touching them will unlock that character, which can be selected from their own menu and has their own unique mechanics and unlocks. Each playable character has a tainted version that can be unlocked this way. If the player changes the character (for example dying with {{T|Missing Poster}} and respawning as {{C|The Lost}}) and re-enters the Hidden Closet, the crying baby will not change to the corresponding character, and will stay as the first character it turned into. This means the player cannot unlock two [[Tainted Characters]] in the same run. In [[Repentance Co-Op|true co-op]], the character in the closet will be the tainted version of player one's character.

If the tainted version of a character has already been unlocked, or a tainted character is being played, the closet will contain {{i|Inner Child}}. If Inner Child has not been unlocked, it will contain a {{E|Shopkeeper}} instead.

The method for obtaining a {{p|Cracked Key}} during the [[ascent]] is described on their respective pages, but {{i|Red Key}} can also be obtained from {{R|Curse Room}}s (if unlocked) or by using {{i|Pandora's Box}} on the Home floor.

Despite rooms in home being full-size, {{i|Red Key}} and {{p|Cracked Key}} cannot be used in any room except the corridor containing the hidden closet.

Therefore any item helping to gain some, such as {{I|Mom's Box}}, will help a lot. Items or pickups that allow to absorb them ({{I|Marbles}}, {{I|Smelter}}, [[Gulp!]]...) are even more important as absorbed trinkets do not take up an item slot. * [[Transformations]] are permanent, and the progress towards transformations by passive items remains if it is replaced with a new item. ** Transformation progress of an item ''will be lost'' if the passive item is removed in any other way, such as being rerolled with{{I|D4}}, or destroyed by {{I|Sacrificial Altar}} * Items that would add items directly to Tainted Isaac (such as {{I|Cambion Conception}}, {{I|Monster Manual}}, etc) or pickups that would do the same (such as {{P|Soul of Lilith}}) do not take up an inventory slot.
